clues.title: Landscape: Cloudless 30C
text: The 18C and 5N road in central Peru, south and east from Pucalipa, and the 30C in eastern Peru, curving up to the Bolivian border, are pretty much the only places in the country with a flat profile (no visible mountains), a well-built road, and lush, jungly vegetation with a slightly yellow tint. You can tell which of the two you're on from the clouds: there aren't really any on the 30C, and the 18C/5N will always have substantial clouds.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Road line: Roadlines
text: Peruvian roads always have white outer lines.
On highways, you will find either single yellow dashed or double yellow middle lines.
On rural mountain roads, you will most likely see white outer lines without any centre line.
In the continent of South America, rural mountain roads, with the features mentioned above, are predominantly found in Peru.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Tumbes

clues.title: Landscape: South Piura Landscape

clues.title: Landscape: Southern Lake Titicaca

clues.title: Landscape: Northern Mountains

clues.title: Landscape: Tarapoto Mountains

clues.title: Landscape: Exposed Rock

clues.title: Landscape: Tall Rocky Mountains

clues.title: Architecture: Architecture - Titicaca Architecture

clues.title: Architecture: North - Overhanging Roofs
text: Buildings with overhanging roofs with wooden supports are mostly found in northern regions of Peru.
These buildings are sometimes brightly coloured as well.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: South - Red Brick Transition
text: As a general rule, the closer you are to Lake Titicaca in Peru, houses and buildings made out of red brick become more common.
This type of architecture resembles the predominant type of building seen in parts of western Bolivia, which is helpful for remembering where it is seen most commonly.
Red brick buildings can be seen anywhere in the country, so use other clues before guessing.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Guardrail: Unique Guardrail
text: Black-and-yellow stripes on guardrails are seen throughout the country. You might sometimes find different designs, such as this sharp arrow design.
NOTE: Similar striped guardrails are also found in Bolivia. To differentiate them, just have a look at the outer stripe. Peru uses a black one, while Bolivia features a yellow one.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Plate: Peru
text: Peruvian licence plates are either white or yellow. In contrast to the white plates, yellow plates are less likely to be seen.

Additionally, taxis in Peru typically use licence plates that are yellow on the top and white on the bottom. A white plate with a yellow stripe on top of the license plate are also seen on taxis, New Jersey and Dominican Republic have this design too.
NOTE: Within South America, yellow licence plates are only found in Peru, Colombia and rarely, Chile.
